dish: Korean fried chicken (original crispy / soy / honey butter), jjajangmyeon, army stew
address: Punggol Coast Hawker Centre, Punggol, Singapore (stall no. + postal to confirm at geocode)
w: A Korean-owned hawker stall in the new Punggol Coast centre frying shatter-crisp Korean chicken by the half or whole (original, sweet-spicy, soy, honey butter), plus jjajangmyeon and army stew — picked by Women's Weekly and Honeycombers among the centre's stalls actually worth eating.

dish: Glutinous rice balls (ah balling) in peanut soup
address: Punggol Coast Hawker Centre, Punggol, Singapore (stall no. + postal to confirm at geocode)
w: The old-school dessert pick at Punggol Coast: comforting bowls of glutinous rice balls served with your choice of soup — named by Women's Weekly and Honeycombers in their centre guides.

address: Punggol Coast Hawker Centre, Punggol, Singapore (stall no. + postal to confirm at geocode)
w: A soy-milk-centric stall that makes its soya milk fresh in-house — the drinks stop Women's Weekly and Honeycombers flag at Punggol Coast.

dish: Signature superior seafood soup (prawns, fish maw, pork slices) with hor fun or you mian, fried fish sticks
w: A homegrown soup specialist since 2011: a sweet-savoury, light seafood broth loaded with prawns, fish maw, pork slices, abalone slices and beancurd-skin fish sticks, over rice, hor fun or you mian — with an addictive chilli and fresh lard. Featured by Eatbook (Punggol guide) and reviewed by Seth Lui.

dish: Australian-style brunch — big brekkie, fluffy pancakes, mushroom chicken chop
w: Punggol's go-to waterfront brunch cafe: Australian-inspired big brekkies, avo toast, soft fluffy pancakes and generous mains like the mushroom chicken chop — picked by Eatbook's Punggol guide and City Nomads' Sengkang–Punggol dining guide.

dish: Fuzhou oyster cake with two whole oysters, minced meat and shrimp; kimchi oyster cake
n: Sixth Floor Oyster Cake (Northshore Plaza) — CLOSED
address: Northshore Plaza I, 407 Northshore Drive #02-41, Singapore
w: A Punggol home business (named for the owner's sixth-floor HDB flat) that grew into a Northshore Plaza kiosk frying ultra-crisp Fuzhou oyster cakes — two whole oysters, minced meat and shrimp — covered by Eatbook and Women's Weekly. CLOSED: both outlets shut permanently after 28 Sep 2025 (Seth Lui).
